label: Late Cretaceous

label: Early Jurassic

label: Late Ordovician

label: Late Ordovician

label: Late Neoproterozoic
explanation: Late Ediacaran.  Strange, soft-bodied Ediacaran organisms such as Dickinsonia and Charnia live on microbial mats on the sea floor.  They are some of the earliest large, complex animals.

label: Late Neoproterozoic

label: Cryogenian
explanation: Cryogenian Period, Marinoan glaciation.  In a "Snowball Earth" episode, ice sheets reach the tropics and sea ice covers most of the ocean.  Life survives in pockets of open water and around volcanic hot springs.

label: Cryogenian
explanation: Cryogenian Period, Sturtian glaciation.  The longest "Snowball Earth" event, lasting from about 717 to 660 million years ago.  Glaciers flow all the way to the equator and most of the ocean is frozen over.

label: Early Neoproterozoic
explanation: Late Tonian.  The supercontinent Rodinia is breaking apart, opening new oceans between its fragments.  Life is microbial, but red and green algae and other single-celled eukaryotes are diversifying in the seas.

label: Early Neoproterozoic
explanation: Tonian Period.  Rodinia begins to rift apart.  The oceans host microbial mats, stromatolites and the first multicellular algae, while the land remains bare rock.
